intro.title: Render Props (MouseTracker)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable MouseTracker component that tracks the mouse cursor position on the screen. You will learn the render props pattern, a technique for sharing state and behavior between components in Vue. The main technologies involved are Vue components, reactive state, and passing functions as props. By the end, you'll create a component that provides mouse coordinates to any UI you design, making your code more flexible and reusable.
intro.usecase: Render props are commonly used in Vue applications when you need to create reusable components that handle specific behaviors while letting parent components control the UI rendering. For example, in interactive dashboards, you might create a `DataFetcher` component that manages API calls and loading states, then passes the data to different chart components via render props. This pattern also appears in form builders where a `FormField` component manages validation logic while allowing custom input rendering, or in drag-and-drop interfaces where a `DraggableArea` handles positioning but lets you render various draggable items. This separation of behavior and presentation makes components more flexible and maintainable across different parts of an application.
